labs.title: Create a Cost-Safe Virtual Warehouse
labs.skill: Warehouse sizing, suspend/resume, and cost control
labs.why_it_matters: SnowPro Core commonly tests warehouse size, auto-suspend, auto-resume, and how warehouse choices affect cost.
labs.scenario: You are setting up a small development warehouse. It must be cheap, safe, and automatically stop when idle.
instructions: Create a warehouse named SB_LAB_WH.
Use XSMALL size.
Set AUTO_SUSPEND to 60 seconds.
Set AUTO_RESUME to TRUE.
Start the warehouse suspended.
labs.input_context: No live Snowflake connection is required in offline mode. Write the SQL you would run in Snowsight.
labs.expected_output: A CREATE OR REPLACE WAREHOUSE statement with the required warehouse properties.
labs.starter_sql: -- Create a cost-safe Snowflake warehouse here
hints: Use CREATE OR REPLACE WAREHOUSE.
AUTO_SUSPEND controls idle shutdown.
INITIALLY_SUSPENDED prevents the warehouse from starting immediately.
labs.solution_sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE WAREHOUSE SB_LAB_WH
  WAREHOUSE_SIZE = XSMALL
  AUTO_SUSPEND = 60
  AUTO_RESUME = TRUE
  INITIALLY_SUSPENDED = TRUE;
exam_traps: A warehouse can burn credits while idle unless AUTO_SUSPEND is configured.
Scaling up and scaling out are different concepts.

labs.title: Query Semi-Structured JSON with VARIANT and FLATTEN
labs.skill: VARIANT, JSON pathing, and FLATTEN
labs.why_it_matters: SnowPro Core frequently tests JSON storage, path extraction, casts, and FLATTEN for arrays.
labs.scenario: You receive purchase events as JSON. Store the payload and return one row per item in the items array.
instructions: Create a table EVENTS_RAW with a VARIANT column.
Insert at least one JSON value using PARSE_JSON.
Select scalar values using path notation.
Use LATERAL FLATTEN to return one row per item.
labs.input_context: Example JSON: {"type":"purchase","customer":{"id":42},"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":2}]}
labs.expected_output: A SELECT that extracts event type/customer id and flattens items into rows.
labs.starter_sql: -- Store and query JSON with VARIANT and FLATTEN
hints: Use VARIANT for semi-structured values.
Use PARSE_JSON for inline JSON strings.
Use LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => payload:items).

validation_tests.name: Uses LATERAL or table function syntax

labs.solution_sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE EVENTS_RAW (EVENT_ID NUMBER, PAYLOAD VARIANT);

INSERT INTO EVENTS_RAW
SELECT 1, PARSE_JSON('{"type":"purchase","customer":{"id":42},"items":[{"sku":"A1","qty":2}]}');

SELECT
  EVENT_ID,
  PAYLOAD:type::STRING AS EVENT_TYPE,
  PAYLOAD:customer.id::NUMBER AS CUSTOMER_ID,
  ITEM.VALUE:sku::STRING AS SKU,
  ITEM.VALUE:qty::NUMBER AS QTY
FROM EVENTS_RAW,
LATERAL FLATTEN(INPUT => PAYLOAD:items) ITEM;
exam_traps: FLATTEN produces rows; JSON path notation extracts fields. They solve different parts of the problem.

labs.title: Design Least-Privilege RBAC

labs.input_context: Assume the warehouse is SB_LAB_WH and the schema is SB_LAB_DB.CORE.
labs.expected_output: Role creation and grant statements implementing least-privilege read access.
hints: Prefer grants to roles, not directly to users.

labs.title: Build Stream + Task MERGE Pipeline
labs.skill: Streams and Tasks for incremental pipelines
labs.why_it_matters: This challenge validates Streams and Tasks for incremental pipelines, which is a key practical skill for advanced-data-engineer.
labs.scenario: Create a stream on a raw table and a scheduled task that merges changes into a target table.
instructions: Create raw and target tables.
Create a stream on the raw table.
Create a task that MERGEs stream rows into target.
Include WHEN MATCHED and WHEN NOT MATCHED behavior.
labs.input_context: Offline mode: write the Snowflake SQL you would run in Snowsight. The app validates SQL structure and key clauses locally.
labs.expected_output: SQL that satisfies all configured validation checks.
hints: Focus on the required Snowflake objects and clauses.
Use clear names with the SB_ prefix so validation can identify your work.
labs.solution_sql:
CREATE OR REPLACE STREAM SB_RAW_STREAM ON TABLE SB_RAW;
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK SB_MERGE_TASK WAREHOUSE = SB_LAB_WH SCHEDULE = '5 MINUTE' AS MERGE INTO SB_TARGET t USING SB_RAW_STREAM s ON t.ID = s.ID WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET t.VALUE = s.VALUE WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (ID, VALUE) VALUES (s.ID, s.VALUE);
labs.teardown_sql: DROP TASK IF EXISTS SB_MERGE_TASK; DROP STREAM IF EXISTS SB_RAW_STREAM;
exam_traps: A stream is consumed when DML reads its change records.

labs.title: Write Snowpark DataFrame Transform
labs.skill: Sessions, DataFrames, and lazy execution
labs.why_it_matters: This challenge validates Sessions, DataFrames, and lazy execution, which is a key practical skill for snowpark.
labs.scenario: Write Snowpark Python that reads a table, filters rows, derives a column, and writes results.
instructions: Use session.table.
Apply filter/select/with_column.
Write to a target table.
Avoid collecting the full dataset to the client.
labs.input_context: Offline mode: write the Snowflake SQL you would run in Snowsight. The app validates SQL structure and key clauses locally.
labs.expected_output: SQL that satisfies all configured validation checks.
hints: Focus on the required Snowflake objects and clauses.
Use clear names with the SB_ prefix so validation can identify your work.
labs.solution_sql:
from snowflake.snowpark.functions import col

def main(session):
    df = session.table("SB_RAW_SALES").filter(col("AMOUNT") > 0).with_column("NET_AMOUNT", col("AMOUNT"))
    df.write.mode("overwrite").save_as_table("SB_CURATED_SALES")
    return "ok"
exam_traps: collect() moves data to the client and can break scalability.
